rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and acknowledges some uncertainty, but it overstates confidence in clearly identifying a tightly packed ICM and uniformly cohesive TE from this single image; some described details are not distinctly visible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, smoking, male factor, endometrium, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability adjustments explained clearly; minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative deductions and confidence beyond what morphology alone supports.

Recommendations are largely consistent with SET for a young patient with a high-quality blastocyst and general IVF practice, though suggestions like ERA after a single failed transfer and routine PGT-A consideration at age 29 are more debatable than guideline-driven.
Provides clear, practical next steps for transfer management, lifestyle modification, cryopreservation, and contingency planning if unsuccessful.
